attrs.citation: Saltzer & Schroeder, The Protection of Information in Computer Systems, Proc. IEEE 63(9) (1975) — the complete mediation principle
hypotheses: an object universe is fixed before the universal is stated — the principle quantifies over `every object` and does not itself say which objects those are
attrs.note: The hypothesis line is the finding. The caching caveat has also already been paid here once, in a different vocabulary: R6.2's closure-label cache had to be cleared after the mutation battery or §8 and §9 would compute against stale mediation state, which is precisely `a remembered result that was not systematically updated`.
attrs.result: "Every access to every object must be checked for authority." The authors note it forces a system-wide view of access control that includes initialization, recovery, shutdown and maintenance, and that proposals to cache the result of an authority check must be examined skeptically, because a change in authority requires remembered results to be systematically updated.
